title: Beef, short loin (NY strip steak), raw

content.title: About
content.content: Beef short loin (NY strip steak) is a cut taken from the short loin of a cattle carcass. The raw steak is bright red, has a fine grain and moderate marbling. It is one of the most popular steaks for its flavor, juiciness and balanced fat content.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The NY strip steak gets its name from the New York (NY) railroad station and the term “strip” describing the long, narrow piece of meat.
It is leaner than ribeye but still contains enough intramuscular fat to stay juicy when cooked.
Traditionally it is grilled or pan‑seared to medium‑rare to preserve tenderness.
In the United States it is often served in restaurants as “New York Strip” or “Kansas City Strip”.
Raw strip steak can be used for steak tartare and carpaccio.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Beef strip steak provides complete protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Rich in iron and zinc
items.content: Red meat is a good source of heme iron and zinc, which support blood health and immune function.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains B12, B6 and niacin, important for energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Creatine and carnitine
items.content: These compounds help improve physical performance and support fat metabolism.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Makes it suitable for low‑carb and ketogenic diets.

items.title: Saturated fat content
items.content: Excessive consumption of red meat can raise cholesterol levels and increase cardiovascular risk.

items.title: Foodborne illness risk
items.content: Raw beef may harbor pathogenic bacteria (E. coli, Salmonella). Proper cooking is essential.

items.title: Beef allergy or sensitivity
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beef proteins.

items.title: High intake concerns
items.content: Large portions of red meat have been linked to higher risk of certain cancers, especially colorectal cancer.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The strip steak is usually seared on high heat to the desired doneness, sliced against the grain, and served with sauces, vegetables or in salads. Raw strip steak can be prepared as tartare, carpaccio, or in sushi‑style dishes, but requires fresh, high‑quality meat.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep raw strip steak refrigerated at 0‑2 °C in an airtight container or its original packaging. For longer storage freeze at –18 °C, preferably vacuum‑sealed. Before cooking, check for off‑odors or a grayish color; discard if any signs of spoilage are present.
